Health Care | Congresswoman Virginia Foxx <tbody> <tr> <td> <div style="text-align: justify;"><img alt="" src="https://farm4.staticflickr.com/3481/3752234057_80a226432f.jpg" style="float: left; border: 2px solid #4f81bd;" width="380" height="300" />With my Republican colleagues, I remain committed to replacing ObamaCare with patient-centered health care that works for the American people.&nbsp;<br /> <br /> That is why I supported the American Health Care Act, a comprehensive replacement of ObamaCare that delivered relief from Obamacare’s taxes and mandates that have hurt job creators, increased premiums, and limited options for patients and health care providers.&nbsp; The bill returns control of health care from Washington back to the states and restores the free market so Americans can access quality, affordable health care options that are tailored to their needs.<br /> <div><br /> Furthermore, I voted for H.R. 1, the Tax Cut and Jobs Act.&nbsp; &nbsp;This bill provides relief from expensive medical bills by expanding the medical expense deduction.&nbsp; H.R. 1 also frees patients from ObamaCare’s individual mandate penalty – allowing the flexibility to buy the health care that’s right for them if they choose.&nbsp;<br /> </div> </div> </td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <div style="text-align: justify;">&nbsp;</div> <div style="text-align: justify;">However, my support for affordable health care options is not limited to replacing Obamacare.&nbsp; Education and Workforce Development | Congresswoman Virginia Foxx <div style="text-align: justify;"><b><u>Education</u>:&nbsp;</b>Achieving and maintaining the highest standards in American education is key to our national competitiveness and to the success of individual Americans.<br /> <br /> </div> <img alt="" src="https://farm3.staticflickr.com/2855/9417336600_0015575c6a_n.jpg" style="float: left; margin-right: 5px; border: 2px solid #4f81bd;" width="280" height="253" /> <div style="text-align: justify;">The United States is home to educational opportunities which have no equal throughout the world. Today's youth must not lose sight of the importance of a good education and should be encouraged to exercise the determination and perseverance required to make the most of the opportunities before them.<br /> <br /> As a parent, grandparent and lifelong educator, I understand how important it is for North Carolinians to know that local teachers have the tools they need to help our children reach their potential. Education is not best when micro-managed at the federal level.&nbsp;<br /> <br /> In recent years, we have taken a positive step forward in restoring local control of our nation’s public schools by passing the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). This historic legislation rolled back the federal footprint on K–12 education and put important decisions about education back where it should be – with parents, teachers and local leaders. The Every Student Succeeds Act was signed into law on December 5, 2015.<br /> <br /> As the Chairwoman of the House Committee on Education &amp; the Workforce, I support education proposals which return decision-making power and resource flexibility to the local level while keeping schools accountable for results to taxpayers, parents, and students.<br /> <div>&nbsp;</div> For more on the Education and Workforce Committee, click <a href="http://edworkforce.house.gov/">here</a>.<br /> </div> </div> <div style="text-align: justify;"><b><u>&lt

National Defense and Veterans | Congresswoman Virginia Foxx <tbody> <tr> <td> <table align="left"> <tbody> <tr> <td><img alt="" src="https://farm9.staticflickr.com/8216/8264099991_5ed28ee557.jpg" style="float: left; margin-right: 5px; border: 2px solid #4f81bd;" /></td> </tr> </tbody> </table> Providing for the common defense of the United States of America is the federal government’s primary duty. The push by the previous administration to shrink the size of our military forces resulted in a readiness crisis that left troops overworked and ill-prepared to face the vast array of threats to America’s security. After nearly a decade of cuts, my colleagues and I have made rebuilding the military one of our top priorities.&nbsp;<br /> <br /> Repairing and rebuilding our military is key to defending our country. Congress is continuing the effort to rebuild our armed forces and ensuring that our brave warfighters have the resources they need to meet current and future threats. I was proud to support the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2019, which will strengthen our military’s readiness, provide our troops with the largest pay raise in eight years, increase the number of uniformed personnel, and ensure that our servicemembers have the equipment and skills necessary to protect our country.&nbsp;<br /> <br /> The entire nation owes our military personnel and veterans a huge debt of gratitude, and we must ensure that debt is properly repaid. One of the ways we have sought to repay that debt is through providing affordable health care for military members and their families, both when in uniform and after they have retired. I am a strong supporter of health care for our veterans and recognize the importance of providing full access to all benefits our veterans have earned, through an easily accessible and affordable system.<br /> <br /> Millions of Americans joined the service with the understanding that health care would be available to them when they retired. Jobs and the Economy | Congresswoman Virginia Foxx <div style="text-align: center;"><img alt="" src="https://farm9.staticflickr.com/8252/8557379055_1512c54712.jpg" style="text-align: left; border: 2px solid #1f497d;" /></div> </div> <p>After one of the worst recession’s in our nation’s history and slowest recovery since World War II, the American people are seeing jobs, opportunity, and confidence come roaring back.</p> <p>After promising a bold agenda called A Better Way, the 115<sup>th</sup> Congress delivered on historic tax cuts, rolling back stifling regulations, revitalizing Main Street by providing relief to community banks, and strengthening career and technical education.&nbsp; We are now witnessing the lowest unemployment rate in decades, increases in take-home pay and extraordinarily high consumer confidence.</p> <p>I have long advocated for a fairer, simpler and lower taxes on American families and job-creators.&nbsp; That’s why I strongly supported H.R. 1, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. &nbsp;This commonsense, historic piece of legislation helped Americans from all walks of life by creating jobs, bolstering paychecks, slashing tax burdens and repatriating American earnings.</p> <p>America previously had one of the worst tax codes in the industrialized world for businesses. By reducing tax rates for businesses large and small, our bill leveled the playing field and made America the jobs magnet of the world.&nbsp; H.R. 1 also threw out special-interest loopholes and consolidated deductions.&nbsp; Most importantly, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act lowered individual tax rates for low- and middle-income Americans and eliminated excessive, costly taxes. That means you get to keep more of your hard-earned paycheck.<br /> </p> <p>To learn more about my support for tax reform, please visit <a href="https://fairandsimple.gop/">https://fairandsimple.gop/</a>.&nbsp;</p> <p>Furthermore, I helped lead the fight to fix Washington through regulatory relief. Energy and Gas Prices | Congresswoman Virginia Foxx <tbody> <tr> <td><img alt="" src="https://farm8.staticflickr.com/7085/7027652181_1c666a2ab7.jpg" width="400" height="268" style="float: left;" />America possesses a wealth of domestic energy reserves, and yet hardworking Americans continue to struggle with unpredictable energy costs. High energy prices reduce consumer purchasing power, slow economic growth, and increase inflation. That is why I support an "all of the above" energy policy to boost domestic energy production so Americans have an affordable, reliable, and diverse energy supply for years to come.&nbsp; <div><br /> Technological advances are making previously untapped energy sources accessible and are fueling America’s energy renaissance. However, even low emitting energy sources are subject to robust scrutiny by federal permitting authorities who are under no deadlines to act and can drag out the approval process for new projects.<br /> <br /> One example of the lengthy approval process is the W. Kerr Scott Damn Hydropower Project. Due to the project requiring extensive coordination with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, there have been delays in the review process for design plans. That is why I sponsored H.R. 951, which extends the deadline for construction to begin on the project and allows the construction license to be reinstated if it expires.&nbsp; This pro-renewable energy legislation was signed into law on July 23, 2018.&nbsp;<br /> <br /> Congress needs to make sure onerous regulatory burdens don’t stand in the way of accessing or advancing all forms of American energy. We must ensure clean air, clean water and a healthy, safe environment based on science, not top-down regulation. Budget and Tax Reform | Congresswoman Virginia Foxx <tbody> <tr> <td><img alt="" src="https://farm8.staticflickr.com/7168/6756796179_0ab5d0b317_m.jpg" style="float: left; margin-right: 5px; border: 2px solid #4f81bd;" width="440" />As American families face financial challenges and work to balance their checkbooks, the federal government should be doing the same.&nbsp; &nbsp;<br /> <br /> Much of the economic turmoil gripping our nation is the result of government spending beyond its means.&nbsp; America needs leaders who abide by principles of sound fiscal management, not those who rush massive, wasteful legislation which excuses waste and exposes taxpayers to fraud and abuse. Immigration | Congresswoman Virginia Foxx <tbody> <tr> <td><img alt="" src="https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wonkblog/files/2013/01/border.jpg" style="float: left; margin-right: 5px; border: 2px solid #4f81bd;" width="306" height="211" /> <div style="text-align: justify;">As the granddaughter of Italian immigrants, I am thankful America has always opened her arms to people looking to build a better way for themselves and their families. But today America’s immigration system is broken. It’s not working for families; it’s not working for employers; it’s not working for taxpayers.&nbsp; We must work to reform our immigration system with humane and common-sense policies.<br /> <br /> Our first principles on immigration reform should be to secure the borders, uphold American laws, and protect our national security.&nbsp; This is why I support enforcing our current immigration laws.&nbsp;&nbsp;<br /> <br /> The incentive for illegal immigration into the United States must also be removed.&nbsp; Workplace enforcement is a critical component to immigration reform. Those who knowingly hire illegal workers are complicit in the broken state of immigration in this country. America currently operates with an optional E-Verify system that allows employers to confirm whether prospective employees are, in fact, legal to hire.
